name: Connecting Ridge (CR1)
description: Ridge connecting the Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Point CR1 (spot 1) of the LOLA illumination study.
published: Illuminated 92 % of the time at 2 m above ground (mean 88.1 %); longest night 4.6 days. 19-year simulation, LOLA 20 m/px.

sources.label: Gläser et al. 2014, EPSC Abstracts 9, EPSC2014-136-1

name: Shackleton Rim (Point A)
description: Point on the rim of Shackleton crater. Complementary to Point B: when one is dark, the other usually has Sun.
published: Illuminated more than 80 % of 2020; together with Point B, more than 94 % of the time. Kaguya topography.

name: Peak near Shackleton (Point D)
description: Small ridge extending from the Shackleton rim along the 120° E meridian. The most illuminated point of the Bussey et al. study.
published: Illuminated 86 % of 2020; longest night ~11.5 days (winter). Mahanti et al. 2024 place an area here (88.79° S, 124.5° E) illuminated ~80 % of the time.

sources.label: Mahanti et al. 2024, Planet. Sci. J. 5, 62

name: De Gerlache Rim (Point C)
description: Point on the rim of de Gerlache crater with stable illumination and the shortest eclipses of the study.
published: Illuminated more than 80 % of 2020; the shortest maximum eclipse of all points studied (~6 days). Kaguya topography.

name: Permanent Shadow (PSR 4)
description: Science-interest zone, not a landing site: it never receives direct sunlight and may contain water ice. Center of the permanently shadowed region SP_889630_1297830.
published: Permanently shadowed region of 6 km² inside the Peak near Shackleton region (Table 1 of the study).

sources.label: Mahanti et al. 2024, Planet. Sci. J. 5, 62

name: Malapert Massif
description: One of the highest mountains of the lunar South Pole, facing the Earth. Outside the regional 3D terrain.
published: Artemis III candidate region in 2022 and 2024. Approximate region coordinate: NASA does not publish a specific point.

sources.label: NASA 2024, Artemis III landing regions update

name: Nobile Crater Rim (Rim 1)
description: Western rim of Nobile crater, next to Mons Mouton. Outside the regional 3D terrain.
published: Artemis III candidate region in 2022 and 2024. Approximate region coordinate: NASA does not publish a specific point.

sources.label: NASA 2024, Artemis III landing regions update
